title_en: Implementation Measures of the State Council on Carrying Out the National Voluntary Tree-Planting Campaign

articles.content_en: 2. Green committees at all levels shall organize and promote all departments and units in their respective regions to widely and deeply publicize the Resolution on Launching a Nationwide Voluntary Tree-Planting Campaign and these Implementing Measures through various forms, propagate the great significance of nationwide tree planting and greening the motherland, earnestly conduct ideological mobilization, raise awareness, create momentum, and ensure that it is known to every household and everyone. At the same time, efforts shall be made to complete preparatory work such as investigation and research, planning and arrangement, seedling cultivation, and technical training, and to carry out the tree-planting campaign in a planned and step-by-step manner, in a down-to-earth and pragmatic way, without resorting to formalism or "one-size-fits-all" practices.

3. All citizens of the People's Republic of China, men aged 11 to 60 and women aged 11 to 55, except for those who have lost the ability to work, shall assume the obligation to perform voluntary tree-planting tasks. Each unit shall truthfully count and report the number of such persons to the local green committee as the basis for allocating specific tasks.
When allocating voluntary tree-planting tasks, the county-level green committee shall determine specific targets in accordance with the requirement of planting three to five trees per person per year, and make flexible and varied arrangements based on local conditions. It may divide responsibility zones by units, undertaking tasks of land preparation, seedling cultivation, planting, and tending; or it may, according to the corresponding labor volume, allocate tasks of a single or several items of afforestation and greening. Such tasks may be determined annually or for a period of several years.
For adolescents aged 11 to 17, they shall be assigned, based on their actual conditions, labor within their capabilities at nearby locations.

4. This voluntary labor shall be limited to the scope under the jurisdiction of the county or city for establishing state-owned forests and collectively-owned forests. Each locality shall, through thorough investigation and research, make unified planning and arrangements for the plots for voluntary tree planting or the projects for participating in greening labor. Cities shall give priority to greening public places such as scenic spots, places of historic interest and scenic beauty, and main streets. Rural areas shall speed up the greening of the "four sides" (house sides, village sides, road sides, water sides) and the construction of farmland shelterbelts. All units such as government organs, organizations, enterprises, schools, and residential areas shall vigorously plant trees, grass, and flowers to beautify the environment.

5. Trees planted on state-owned land using voluntary labor shall belong to the unit currently managing and operating the land; if there is no clearly designated management unit, they shall belong to the department or unit designated by the local government. Trees voluntarily planted on collectively-owned land shall belong to the collective unit. If special circumstances exist and other agreements or contracts have been made, such matters shall be handled according to the agreements or contracts. For units owning such trees, people's governments at or above the county level shall issue certificates to effectively protect their legitimate rights and interests.

6. To ensure the seedlings needed for voluntary tree planting, all localities shall make efforts to run existing state-owned nurseries and collective nurseries well, allocate necessary amounts of land and professional personnel, expand and establish new seedling bases, and cultivate improved varieties and strong seedlings. All units that have conditions shall actively establish their own nurseries. Urban households and rural members are encouraged to carry out nutrient pot seedling cultivation.

7. The cultivation, protection, and management of voluntarily planted trees and existing forests must be vigorously strengthened to ensure survival and forest formation and to prevent damage. The units that own the trees or assume the obligation of protection and management shall, according to circumstances, organize forest farms, professional teams, or designate specific persons to take charge of protection and management. Legal systems and discipline shall be strictly enforced, and village regulations and folk conventions for loving and protecting forests shall be established. Harvesting and regeneration must be approved by the forestry or garden department in accordance with the provisions of the Forest Law. Urban green spaces shall be strictly protected and shall not be occupied or damaged. Violators shall be subject to economic penalties or legal sanctions.

8. Tree planting and greening shall be science-based and focused on practical results. Technical backbone personnel shall be trained, technical guidance shall be strengthened, technical knowledge of tree planting and greening shall be popularized, and operations shall be strictly carried out in accordance with technical regulations to ensure quality.

9. With respect to voluntary tree planting, each unit shall conduct inspections annually and truthfully report the completion status. The green committee shall regularly organize appraisals; those with outstanding achievements shall be commended and rewarded. For adult citizens aged 18 or above who fail to perform this obligation without valid reason, their units shall give criticism and education, order them to replant within a time limit, or impose economic penalties. If a whole unit fails to complete the task, the leadership responsibility shall be pursued, and the local green committee shall collect a certain amount of greening fee.

10. Forestry and garden departments at all levels shall, under the leadership of green committees, work together with relevant departments to diligently carry out specific work such as planning, design, and seedling cultivation. If grassroots institutions are not well established, they shall be strengthened and reinforced.

11. The costs for seedlings and for protection and management required for voluntary tree planting shall, in accordance with the principle of self-reliance and frugality, generally be borne by the unit that owns the trees. For units that have heavy greening tasks and financial difficulties and are truly unable to bear all the costs, the costs shall be resolved by the fiscal authorities at all levels according to the subordinate relationship of the units. Transportation and other expenses needed by units and individuals participating in voluntary tree planting shall be borne by the participating units themselves.

12. Carrying out the nationwide voluntary tree-planting campaign is a major measure to promote overall afforestation and greening. When carrying out this campaign, all localities must combine it with accelerating the overall afforestation and greening work, and make overall arrangements in terms of the use of seedlings, funds, technical force, and forest management and protection, so as to both carry out voluntary tree planting well and complete the annual afforestation and greening plan. For a locality that has completed the voluntary tree-planting task but has not done a good job in overall afforestation and greening, it shall not be commended or rewarded.

13. In accordance with the provisions of the Resolution on Launching a Nationwide Voluntary Tree-Planting Campaign and these Implementing Measures, the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate detailed implementation rules in light of actual conditions.
Measures for officers and soldiers of the People's Liberation Army to participate in voluntary tree planting outside military camps shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the "Instruction on the Participation of the Military in Voluntary Tree Planting Outside Camps" (Document No. 3 of 1982) issued by the State Council and the Central Military Commission; measures for tree planting inside camps shall be separately formulated by the General Headquarters of the PLA. However, the local people's governments must cooperate closely, make reasonable plans, and help the military solve the practical problems that should be solved.
